ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a transition-state structure with curved arrows. The main body is a bicyclic skeleton in which a benzene ring is fused with a five-membered nitrogen-containing ring; there is an N-H in the five-membered ring, and there is also a C-H at the top. A CO2H substituent is attached on the right, shown as ring carbon—carboxyl carbon, carboxyl carbon=oxygen, and carboxyl carbon—OH. There is also a positive charge symbol and a reaction arrow in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows and excluding all bonds involving hydrogen. Reasoning: Count only bonds between non-hydrogen atoms. According to the specified method, in the fused bicyclic core, the benzene six-membered ring provides 6 heavy-atom ring connections; after removing the fused edge shared with the benzene ring, the fused five-membered ring additionally provides 4 heavy-atom connections, so the core has 10 heavy-atom bonds in total. The carboxyl substituent on the right further contributes 3 heavy-atom bonds: ring carbon—carboxyl carbon 1, carbonyl C=O 1, and carboxyl C—O 1. Exclude the top C-H, N-H, O-H, and all arrows. The total is 10 + 3 = 13.

method.method_draft: First inspect the image and mark only bonds between non-hydrogen atoms. Count the fused bicyclic core by edges: the benzene six-membered ring contributes 6 heavy-atom ring connections, and the fused five-membered ring contributes 4 additional heavy-atom connections beyond the shared fused edge, giving 10 ring/core bonds. Then count the substituent at the right: the bond from the ring carbon to the carboxyl carbon, the carbonyl C=O bond, and the C-O bond to OH, giving 3 more. Exclude the top C-H, the N-H, the O-H, and all arrows. Add 10 + 3 to obtain 13.

method.method_draft: Inspect the structure and assign a heavy-atom degree to each non-H atom from the drawing. Around the fused ring, the six benzene carbons and the atoms of the five-membered ring give a total heavy-atom incidence count of 20 for the core connections, corresponding to 10 core bonds. For the right-hand CO2H substituent, add the incidences for the ring-to-carboxyl bond and the two C-O connections: these 3 bonds contribute 6 more incidences.
